properties.description:
CONFORMANCE OF AN IMPLEMENTATION AGAINST A PUBLISHED CONTRACT, which is what a check on an Interface asserts and what a check on a Capability does not. `ifc:mcp-tools` promises that `tools/list` returns every served tool with its JSON Schema, and that the field-level contract "travels with the surface and cannot drift from the build". This is the check that the promise is still kept: one committed golden per tool in `tools/toolsnaps/`, holding the WHOLE served object — name, description, inputSchema, annotations — compared against the live binary driven over real stdio. 155 goldens as of 2026-08-22. A real surface change becomes a deliberate `--update` that shows up in the diff, named tool by tool.

IT DRIVES THE BUILT BINARY OVER REAL STDIO rather than an in-process client, on AGENTS.md's rule that every other layer is a client we wrote and only the shipped wire format is trustworthy. That is also why it verifies THIS boundary: the stdio transport is the one it actually speaks.

═══ WHY IT EXISTS: a bug FAMILY, not a worry ═══
Three defects where the surface an agent binds to changed and nothing noticed — a parameter lost its type (BL-28), a stale binary served an old shape (BL-32), prose moved into the wrong envelope (BL-48). The gate turned that family into a mechanical tripwire.

═══ WHAT THIS GREEN DOES NOT COVER, so it is not read wider than it is ═══
· NOT THE HTTP BOUNDARY. It speaks stdio, so it says nothing about `ifc:mcp-tools-http` — which remains unchecked, and is the half flo2's `ifc:reflow2-design-api` actually pairs with.
· NOT THE ERROR MODEL. `ifc:mcp-tools` specifies TWO layers a consumer must handle — JSON-RPC transport `error`, and tool-level failure as a normal result carrying `isError: true` — and a golden of the `tools/list` payload cannot see either. The most expensive defect this project has had (v0.38.0 shipping an empty manifest) was precisely a caller reading a reply's shape and not its content, and this check would not have caught it.
· NOT WHETHER THE SCHEMA IS RIGHT — only that it has not moved. A wrong shape frozen on day one stays green forever.

═══ THE GATE'S OWN DEFECT, found and fixed 2026-08-16 ═══
It defaulted `--bin` to `target/debug/reflow2-mcp` and reported "ALL 149 TOOLSNAPS MATCH" against whatever stale build was sitting there — a check that could not fail reporting a pass, the shape this project keeps finding. CI was never exposed (ci.yml builds debug in the same job first), so it was a local-developer defect and specifically bit whoever followed the RELEASE PROCEDURE, which builds release and leaves debug behind. Fixed by `chg:the-surface-gate-says-which-binary-it-read`: every verdict now NAMES the binary and its build time and warns when any source is newer. The default must stay debug, because CI builds debug.
properties.findings:
ALL 155 TOOLSNAPS MATCH — the served surface is unchanged. Run 2026-08-22 against target/debug/reflow2-mcp, and THE VERDICT NAMED THE BINARY AND ITS BUILD TIME, which is `chg:the-surface-gate-says-which-binary-it-read` visibly working: before that fix this gate reported "ALL 149 MATCH" against a stale build and could not fail.

SECOND RUN THE SAME DAY REPORTED DRIFT (2), AND THAT WAS THE POINT. Adding `documentation` to ChangeType changed two served descriptions — `add_change_event`'s tool description and `set_artifact_checksum`'s `change_type` parameter. The gate named both, they were blessed with `--update`, and the diff shows exactly what moved. A deliberate surface change is therefore distinguishable from drift, which is the whole reason the goldens are committed.

WHAT THIS GREEN DOES NOT SAY, restated because a passing check gets quoted wider than it is: nothing about `ifc:mcp-tools-http` (this drives stdio), nothing about the two-layer error model (a `tools/list` golden cannot see `isError`), and nothing about whether the frozen schemas are RIGHT — only that they have not moved.
properties.name: Every served tool's name, prose, schema and annotations match a committed golden (tools/toolsnap.py, CI on every push)
